name: Strangers after 4 weeks' proximity: stimulus partner, 6 CCW fields, reversed (Persinger 2008)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008), circumcerebral 'Octopus' ring, paired-stranger design
summary: The stimulus partner's program from Persinger et al. 2008, in the reverse order half the pairs got: six 5-min counter-clockwise ring configurations (three burst-firing, three Thomas) after the two strangers had met twice a week for four weeks. The paper reports more power in a narrow theta band in the unexposed partner during the frequency-modulated field its text calls '20 msec (+2 msec)' (phase 3 here), in 4 pairs.
notes: Persinger 2008: 8 student volunteers met in pairs twice a week for 4 weeks, within 2 m of each other (p.4 [10]). Table 1 (p.5 [11]), played here as printed: burst-firing 1/1/20/+2, 1/2/100/+20, 3/3000/200/-2; frequency-modulated 1/1/20/-2, 2/1/100/+20, 3/3000/200/-2 (point duration / gap / time on coil 1 / change per coil, ms). Half of the stimulus persons received the patterns from left to right, half in reverse (p.5 [11]): this program plays the reverse order, persinger-strangers-2008 the table order. The 2-ms gap (BF2) and 2-ms points (FM2) differ from the 2002 and 2003 tables the paper says it repeats and may be misprints. Signs follow the paper's own text: plus means shorter at each next coil, so the rows play 20 to 6 ms, 100 to 20 ms and 200 to 214 ms. Cook 1999 reads the same table the other way (p.3 [63]). The paper itself is not consistent: its table prints -2 for FM1 while its text calls that field '20 msec (+2 msec)' and an acceleration (p.7 [13]), and its discussion has the +20 pattern decrease from 100 ms (p.10 [16]). FM1 follows the text here: 20 down to 6 ms. Thomas plays from the 849-point patent table; the burst-firing values were never published, so the project's rising sweep stands in. One coil at a time, counter-clockwise from Fp1 to Fp2 (site names are this project's reading). Only the stimulus partner wears a helmet: one helmet delivers the whole magnetic exposure. The paper gives 1.5 uT within 1 cm of the ring's perimeter and 0.5 uT at its centre (p.4 [10]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT the scalp gets about 24 uT and the ring centre roughly 0.02 uT. 4 pairs, many statistical tests, no independent replication. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Both partners must agree to the experiment; do not use results for decisions about real people. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on distress.
setting: Stimulus partner (this helmet): blindfolded, seated in a quiet, dark room (the lab used an acoustic chamber), imagining being with the partner, the instruction of the lab's sibling study. Response partner: another room, blindfolded with earplugs, no helmet, EEG recorded (the outcome measure); whoever scores the EEG should not know the phase times.
schedule: First the two meet twice a week for 1 h for 4 weeks, staying within 2 m of each other (the paper's Method; its abstract says one metre); then one 30-min session. For a self-test, add a session on the app's Blind option (real or sham at random) and score the EEG or the partner's reports before unblinding.
source: Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008, Enhanced power within a predicted narrow band of theta activity during stimulation of another by circumcerebral weak magnetic fields after weekly spatial proximity: evidence for macroscopic quantum entanglement?, NeuroQuantology 6(1):7-21 https://doi.org/10.14704/nq.2008.6.1.151 ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, Theoretical and experimental evidence of macroscopic entanglement between human brain activity and photon emissions, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (20+2 notation; coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003, Percept Mot Skills 97:877-894 (sibling pairs) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14738355/ ; Lehman 2016, PhD thesis, Laurentian University ("20-2" = 20, 22 ... 34 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/e7b03302-1b7f-4f4f-acf5-bdf41ee5370f/content ; Koren & Persinger, US 6,312,376 B1 (sequence interval and sequence acceleration) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6312376B1/en ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse point values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University (230-point burst-firing file) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Booth, Koren & Persinger 2008, Electromagn Biol Med 27:426-436 (counter-clockwise vs clockwise) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19037792/ ; Cook, Koren & Persinger 1999, Neurosci Lett 268:61-64 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10400078/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
